title: BatchEnsemble rank-one vs Mirror task ensemble views
hypothesis: A per-member orthogonal input-view address preserves task-member quality on a low-dimensional classifier orbit at fewer bytes than BatchEnsemble rank-one factors.
physical_object: One shared binary linear classifier vector

development.selection_metric: aligned accuracy and actual payload bytes

optimization.classifier_fit: convex logistic regression via scipy L-BFGS
optimization.representation_fit: least squares on fitted member separator vectors

storage.serializer: uncompressed NumPy NPZ preserving learned dtype

compute.active_compute_proxy: classifier fit examples and dense inference multiply proxy; representation decode work separately disclosed

success_gate: On at least 3/4 fresh aligned seeds, Mirror within 1 accuracy point and 2 disagreement points of independent while using <=25% BatchEnsemble bytes.
failure_gate: On at least 3/4 fresh seeds, aligned Mirror loses >5 accuracy points, or uses more bytes than BatchEnsemble for quality within 1 point.
boundaries: unaligned stress set is a scope test
runtime not compared because decode kernels are unoptimized
